newsitem.title: JAPAN: Zinc--Japan traders say smelters cut GSP buying.
newsitem.headline: Zinc--Japan traders say smelters cut GSP buying.

text.p: Japanese smelters have reduced their contracted volume of Chinese zinc purchases for import next year under the General System of Preferences (GSP) scheme, Japanese trade sources said on Tuesday.

They estimated this year's volume at 15,000 to 20,000 tonnes, compared with more than 30,000 tonnes last year, while this year's premiums were said to have been set at about $100 a tonne on a CIF basis over London Metal Exchange cash prices.
A source at a Japanese smelter declined to comment on the talk of the purchases, although he said that less Chinese zinc was expected to be available next year for import to Japan.
"Premiums are high in Southeast Asia," he said. "(China's zinc) will probably flow in that direction."

Trade and industry sources also said that Japan's total amount of GSP zinc purchases for next year was likely to drop from this year's heavy 82,535 tonnes, noting that the pending closure of two Japanese zinc smelters had spurred overbuying.
The GSP scheme extends tariff exemptions to metal imports from developing countries submitted for customs clearance at the start of the fiscal year on April 1.

Trade sources said Japan's smelters, which supply both imported zinc and their own domestic production to their customers, base their import decisions on a number of factors, including domestic availability.
They added, however, that Japanese smelters have a strategic incentive to conclude purchase contracts early, usually during the summer, and little incentive to haggle for low premiums.

Trade houses and end users are expected to begin talks in October on next year's GSP-related zinc imports, and if some deals were already concluded at generous premiums, Chinese producers would be reluctant to sell metal more cheaply to other Japanese buyers, the sources said.
In the first seven months of calendar year 1996, China accounted for 55.2 percent of Japan's 115,941 tonnes of refined zinc imports.

As of May 30, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry estimated that Japan's zinc imports in the April 1996/March 1997 fiscal year would rise to 172,000 tonnes from 112,300 tonnes, while domestic production was expected to total 581,000 tonnes, down from 660,000 tonnes the year before.
Demand was expected to dip slightly to 658,000 tonnes from 662,300 tonnes. --Tokyo Commodities Desk (81-3 3432 6179)
